summary: Seiji Nemoto studied at Meiji University (~1968–1972) and worked in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Japanology. He served as a professor at the University of Tsukuba from around 2003 to 2015.
Seiji Tanaka studied under Bruno Petzold. During his academic career, he held posts at Aoyama Gakuin University (~1968–1980) and Asia University (~1980–1988).
Seijun Ishii studied at Komazawa University from around 1977 to 1987. Working in the field of Buddhist studies, he became a professor at Komazawa University around 2003.

Seikaku Hirata was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1946–1949) under Shin'ichi Hisamatsu, as well as under Bokuo Seki. He held a post at Hanazono University from around 1969 to 2000.

Sein Tin studied at Basic Education High School No. 9 Mawlamyine, the University of Rangoon (~1918–1923), under Pe Maung Tin (1924–1927), and at Christ Church (~1927–1930). He was active in linguistics.

Seiran Ouchi was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who founded Hoshi Sodan (1874) and Meikyo Shinshi (1875). He held a post at Nishi Hongan-ji and served as president of Toyo University from 1914 to 1918.

Seiren Matsunami studied at the University of Tokyo (until 1930) under Naoshiro Tsuji and Walther Schubring. A specialist in Indology and Buddhist studies, he held posts at Kyushu University (attested 1965, 1979), Taisho University (1972), and Rissho University (1972).

A scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology, Karashima studied at the University of Tokyo, Cambridge, and Peking University under mentors including von Hinüber and Ji Xianlin. He held posts at the Eastern Institute and Soka University (~1996–2019).

Seishin Kato studied at Toyo University and Shingiyaha Daigakurin. Active in Buddhist studies, he served as professor and president of Buzan University, professor and president of Toyo University, and president of Taisho University.
Seitatsu Matsunami worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He served as an assistant at the University of Tokyo and as a professor at Taisho University (attested 1992).

A scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, Yanagida studied at Hanazono, Otani, and Kyoto Universities under Shin'ichi Hisamatsu. He held posts at Hanazono University (1949–1995), Kyoto University (1976–1986), and Chubu University (~1988–1994).

Sempa Dorje is a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied under Ram Shankar Tripathi. He served as a professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1977, 1990–1998).
Sen Wang studied at Peking University from around 1931 to 1935. Working in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, he held a professorship at Minzu University of China from around 1952 to 1985.

Senarat Wijayasundara worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. In 1999, he was attested as a teacher at the University of Kelaniya and as a visiting lecturer at the Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore.
Senarath Paranavitana worked in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He succeeded Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe and held a post at Leiden University.
Senchu Murano studied Buddhist studies at Rissho University (~1930–1933) and the University of Washington (~1934–1938). He later served as a professor at Rissho University from around 1952 to 1978.

Sengaku Mayeda studied at the University of Tokyo, Pennsylvania, and Münster under W. Norman Brown, Hajime Nakamura, and Frits Staal. Active in Indology and philosophy, he held posts at Pennsylvania, the University of Tokyo, and Musashino University.

Senkyo Sakawa studied at Rissho University (completed ~1965) and worked in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He served at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra and as a professor at Rissho University.

Senmyo Naniwa earned a PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University and studied under Genjun Sasaki, Mohan G. Dhadphale, J. R. Joshi, and P. V. Bapat. In 2005, he was a researcher at Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute and professor at Bukkyo University.
Sensho Kimura studied at Otani University from around 1962 to 1971. Working in Buddhist studies and Sinology, he later served as a professor at Otani University from around 1988 to 2008.
